function.name: working_memory_put
function.description: Save a string in this session's temporary working memory under a new, literal key. An occupied key is an error. Use a new key for processed results. format is an optional text/json label; JSON is not parsed or validated.

function.name: working_memory_get
function.description: Read the complete string at a working-memory key into your context, even if large. Use only when you need the full content yourself; input_refs on invoke_sub_agent passes data directly to a child without loading it here. Missing keys are errors.

function.name: working_memory_list
function.description: List this session's working-memory keys, formats and UTF-8 sizes without loading their contents.

function.name: working_memory_delete
function.description: Delete a working-memory key from this session. Returns deleted=false if absent. Deletion affects all loops sharing this session; past message contents remain in their histories.

function.name: set_memory
function.description: Persist a small piece of agent-side state to the local memory KV. Use for watermarks, last-seen markers, counters, or any note the agent wants to recall in a future session. Well-known keys (e.g. `news_digest.last_read_at`) are auto-injected into the `Current context` block of future system prompts. Values are stored as strings — JSON-stringify complex payloads yourself.

value.description: Value to store. Use ISO timestamps for time markers.

function.name: code_agent
function.description: Delegate a computational / coding task to a sandboxed code agent (Codex). It writes AND runs code (Python with pandas/openpyxl, or Node) and returns ONLY the final result. Use it for anything that must be COMPUTED rather than recalled or written by an LLM: exact arithmetic, counting, date/time math, statistics, parsing or aggregating CSV/Excel/JSON data, string/data transformations, regex extraction, unit conversions. Do NOT use it for web access, reasoning, or composing prose — only code/computation. State the task precisely and say exactly what the output should be (e.g. 'return just the number'). Put any data the code needs in `data` — it is delivered to the program on stdin (for a binary file like .xlsx, base64-encode it and say so in the task).

task.description: Precise description of the computation to perform and the exact output expected. E.g. 'Sum the `total` column of the CSV on stdin; return only the rounded integer.'

data.description: Optional input data delivered to the program on stdin (CSV/JSON/numbers/text, or base64 for a binary file). Omit if the task is self-contained.

function.name: read_skill
function.description: Read a skill to use its instructions in this session. Returns effective live/default text with improver patches, tools and content_hash. Does not execute the skill or grant additional tool permissions. Pass expected_hash from find_skills to reject a changed version. If required tools are unavailable here, delegate to a worker with that named skill. Follow effectiveInstructions; editableBody is the unpatched body for revisions and tools/routable are its metadata.

name.description: Skill name without .md extension (matches signal source).

function.name: write_skill
function.description: Create or replace an agent-managed skill in the persistent live overlay, outside Git. Use when the user asks to save or change standing instructions. Supply the full Markdown file with YAML frontmatter (tools: * or a tool list, routable: true for discoverable skills) and a first paragraph explaining when it applies. When revising, read first and use editableBody with the returned tools/routable metadata to avoid copying improver patches. Live changes are available to find_skills immediately; the description index catches up later. A live-only skill has no shipped fallback.

content.description: Full new content of the skill file.

function.name: list_skills
function.description: List all available skills (union of live overlay + shipped defaults). Each entry includes `source: 'live'|'default'` showing which layer is active for that name. Useful for the `dreaming` skill to survey what's edit-able before deciding what to revise.

function.name: invoke_sub_agent
function.description: Delegate a focused subtask when useful or when required tools are unavailable here. The worker loads only the named skills, without parent history, and returns its result through shared working memory. Small results include content; large ones include memory_key and preview. Give it the relevant context and delivery role. Its side effects take effect immediately: do not duplicate a reply already sent by a worker. Reading a skill does not require delegation.

skills.description: Skill names to load in the sub-agent (e.g. ["news-digest"]). Optional; omit or use [] for a general-purpose focused worker with all MCP tools. Named skills restrict its MCP tools. No engine meta-skills or parent history are copied.

system_prompt.description: Optional goal / framing / constraints the PARENT wants the sub-agent to follow on top of its skill. Goes into the sub-agent's system message ahead of the skill content. Use this to set scope ("only fetch X, not Y"), output format ("return JSON", "reply in Russian"), delivery target ("send to chat=<id> thread=<n>"), or any other context the skill itself doesn't know about. Skip when the skill is self-sufficient.

prompt.description: Task / user-facing request to hand to the sub-agent — goes in as a user message and shows up as the sub-agent's trace input. Use the user's verbatim wording when possible. For self-initiated tasks (no user message) put the trigger description here.

input_refs.description: Optional working-memory keys. Their complete contents are loaded directly into the sub-agent's user message as data, without entering the parent's context. Parent and child share the same working memory.

max_iterations.description: Optional iteration budget for the sub-agent. Default 50.

preset.description: Model preset for the sub-agent. `base` — cheap chat model, no thinking (default; use for simple one-offs and lookups). `smart` — DeepSeek with thinking on (use for real editorial / parsing work: digests, semantic dedup, PDF amount extraction). Default `base`.

function.name: save_workflow
function.description: Validate a saved-workflow definition (Open Workflow Specification DSL 1.0, YAML) and store it as a new draft version of `name`. Problems come back with the path of the task and property to fix; fix them all and save again. The reply lists every call the workflow makes with its effect (read/write) — show the user the write calls before asking them to confirm. A draft never runs; see activate_workflow.

name.description: The workflow's name; must equal document.name in the definition.

note.description: What this version changes, for the history.

function.name: activate_workflow
function.description: Make a saved version of a workflow the one that runs; the version active before retires. Call it ONLY after the user explicitly confirmed this version in the chat. A task scheduled with schedule_task(workflow: name) then runs it without the agent.

function.name: list_workflows
function.description: List saved workflows: the newest version of each, its status, and which version is active.

function.name: read_workflow
function.description: Read a saved workflow's definition: the newest version, or `version`.

function.name: schedule_task
function.description: Register a cron-driven task. When the cron matches, the agent gets a `scheduler` signal with the given prompt and acts on it (send a Telegram message, run a check, etc). Cron is standard 5-field (minute hour day-of-month month day-of-week) evaluated in the user's configured timezone. For one-shot reminders set `recurring: false` and use a specific cron like '30 14 12 5 *' (14:30 on May 12); the task auto-deactivates after the first fire. For repeating tasks use a generic cron like '0 9 * * *' (every day 9:00). Convert natural-language times into cron syntax before calling this tool. To run something once right away ("прогони сейчас"), set `cron_expr: "now"`: it fires within half a minute, after the current conversation turn ends. With `workflow`, each fire runs that saved workflow's active version instead of planning the task.

cron_expr.description: 5-field cron: minute hour day-of-month month day-of-week; or "now" to fire once right away.

prompt.description: What the fire asks the agent to do (the signal's text).

workflow.description: A saved workflow with an active version to run on each fire.

function.name: list_scheduled_tasks
function.description: Show every task that may still fire — recurring tasks (always) and one-shots that haven't been triggered yet. Each row includes the cron expression, prompt, the saved workflow it runs (if any), last fire time, and the next 1-3 upcoming fire timestamps in the user's timezone for sanity-checking.

function.name: cancel_scheduled_task
function.description: Permanently remove a task by id. Use this when the user says 'forget about that reminder' or 'stop the daily X'. Returns { ok: true, id } on success, { ok: false, id } if no such task.

function.name: workflow_functions
function.description: The functions a saved workflow can call, one line each: name, arguments (`?` optional), read or write, a one-line summary. With `name`, that one function in full: its description and argument schema.

name.description: One function to show in full.

function.name: probe_function
function.description: Run one read function of a workflow once, with these arguments, and see its reply (cut to its first few thousand characters). Build a definition's expressions from the fields of this reply. Functions that change something and model steps are refused.

arguments.description: The arguments as the workflow's `with` would pass them.

function.name: try_workflow
function.description: Dry-run a saved workflow version once, now, as a scheduled fire would run it: reads and model steps run for real on today's data, while every write (a message, a watermark, a journal entry) is only recorded with its arguments, so nothing changes. Returns the steps with their outputs, the writes it would have made and how the run ended.

version.description: The version to run; the latest saved one by default.

function.name: hash_value
function.description: Compute SHA-256 of canonical JSON; object key order does not affect the hash.

function.name: skill_catalog_snapshot
function.description: Return all active skills as {skills:[{name,content,content_hash,routable,tools}]}. Content includes live/default resolution and improver patches. Hashes cover effective instructions and execution metadata. No model calls or writes.

function.name: find_skills
function.description: Discover skills useful for the current request through the agent decision client. Include signal source and delivery channel in context. Independently scores every routable live/default skill from 0 to 1, filters and sorts, then returns names, descriptions, scores and content_hash. Read applicable communication and domain skills with read_skill and expected_hash. New or changed skills use their current first paragraph until the index catches up. Does not execute skills or grant permissions.
